title: I Wrote One Sentence a Day for a Year. Here's What Changed.
creator: Hollis Grey
description:
365 days, one sentence each. What I expected, what actually happened, and the entries I almost deleted.

The app I used for this whole project, Notebloom, sponsored this video. Get 30% off a year of Premium at notebloom.app/hollis

Books mentioned:
The Artist's Way
Register of Days (fiction)

sentences.t: Last October I made a really small promise to myself.
Write one sentence a day, every day, for a year.
Not a journal, not a diary, just one sentence about the day I'd just had.
I figured I'd give up by December, like I give up on basically everything I start in the autumn.
But I didn't, and three hundred and sixty five sentences later, I want to talk about what that did to my head.
The first month was terrible, honestly.
My sentences were things like, went to work, it rained.
Tired, ate soup.
I'd write them at eleven fifty nine at night, half asleep, just so I didn't break the streak.
And then, somewhere in November, something shifted.
I started noticing things during the day and thinking, oh, that could be the sentence.
The man on the bus who was teaching his daughter to whistle.
The way the light hit the kitchen at four o'clock.
I wasn't writing more, but I was paying more attention, and that turned out to be the whole point.
I should mention that I did this whole thing in an app called Notebloom, and they're actually sponsoring this video.
I tried a paper notebook first and lost it in a week, so I needed something that lives on my phone and nags me gently at nine p m.
Notebloom is a journaling app that's built for exactly this, short daily entries, streaks, and a little calendar where every day you write turns into a flower.
By the end of the year my calendar looked like a garden, and I'm not ashamed to say that was very motivating.
It also has a feature called on this day, so you can see what you wrote a month ago, or a year ago.
You can try it free, and if you go to notebloom dot app slash hollis, you get thirty percent off a year of Premium.
Again, that's notebloom dot app slash hollis.
So, what changed?
The biggest one is memory.
I can now tell you something specific about almost every day of the past year, which I genuinely could not do before.
Before this, a whole month could vanish, and I'd only remember that it was February and I was cold.
The second thing is that bad days got smaller.
When you have to sum up a bad day in one sentence, it kind of forces you to put a frame around it.
Like, in March, I wrote, Got the rejection email, made pancakes anyway.
And reading that back, I'm proud of that person.
The third thing surprised me, which is that I started to like my own life more.
Not because anything big happened, it was a pretty ordinary year, but because I had proof that it was full of good small things.
There were a few entries I nearly deleted, I'll be honest.
There's a week in June that's just the word fine over and over, and I know exactly what that week was.
But I kept them, because that's true too.
I'm going to keep going, by the way, year two started last week.
And thanks again to Notebloom for sponsoring this, if you want to try your own year of sentences, you get thirty percent off Premium at notebloom dot app slash hollis.
If you do start, tell me your first sentence in the comments, I'd love to read them.
Bye for now.
